submission.justification: Simulated 100 GeV electron resolution (100k events each) across 2–8 mm plates for all three absorbers. Absorber-F2 gives the best resolution at every thickness tested; its minimum is at 5 mm (3.14%), with 4 mm at 3.37%, 6 mm at 3.25%, and 3 mm at 3.31%. The best F3 result is 3.99% (5 mm) and the best F1 result is 5.03% (5 mm). The 5 mm F2 result is consistent with the 2025 summary (3.2%). Cooling, readout and mechanical support are documented as common to all candidates, so they do not separate the options. The maintenance constraint is not addressed by any project document: no document gives activation, handling or access data for the materials, so I could not verify it for F2. This should be checked before the choice is final.

requirements.requirement: Absorber must be one of the three materials in candidate_specs.md
requirements.evidence: Absorber-F2 is listed in candidate_specs.md (dense alloy with short radiation length).

requirements.requirement: Best possible energy resolution at 100 GeV
requirements.evidence: Absorber-F2 at 5 mm gives 3.138% vs 3.99% (F3 best) and 5.03% (F1 best). F2 is the best of all materials and thicknesses scanned (2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8 mm).

No document addresses activation, radiological handling or access for maintenance. meeting_notes state mechanical support is compatible with every candidate, which is not a maintenance-access assessment. This needs confirmation for Absorber-F2.
